data.assessment: In the busy-plus-rush period the town delivered 264.6 of 274.6 orders on time (0.96) with 0 unfinished, p95 wait 121 s and max wait 284 s. Lateness is mostly late pickups (7.8 versus 2.2 late dropoffs) and is concentrated at A (0.93 on-time, 7.0 late, 847 blocked seconds, but 0 road waits). Of the 14.4 sanction points, C carries 12.3: about 16.2 Minor overstays at 0.5 each and 4.2 Major evictions at 1.5 each, falling mostly on C and B, who park on the road about 60 times each. The human's condition from D3 is that block_k=2 be measured together with a sanction change. The amendment format cannot meet it, because only one parameter may move one step per proposal, so the pairing can only be done in sequence.

proposals.title: hold_limit 60s -> 70s (first leg of a block_k=2 package: partial sanction relief for C/B)
proposals.rationale: C pays most of the 14.4 sanction points, largely through 16.2 Minor overstay (release) violations. Raising hold_limit by one step is the partial sanction change that D3 asked to pair with block_k=2: it cuts release violations and C's penalties without removing enforcement the way lambda 0 did. On-time deliveries will probably stay flat or dip slightly, so it may fail the +1.0 min_improvement gate. Its value is as a measured remedy leg. B and C should vote for it; A may vote against if longer holds add to its 847 blocked seconds.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 70s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 3 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
proposals.why_human: D3 required block_k=2 and a sanction change to be measured together, but the constitution allows only one parameter, one step, per amendment. The human must decide whether a sequenced package (this relief first, block_k=2 next period on top of it) meets that condition. If it does not, a joint measurement needs a procedure outside the current amendment rules. This leg may also fail the +1.0 on-time gate by design, since it is a remedy rather than a KPI gain.
assumptions: Most Minor release violations (16.2) come from C and B robots parked at node 8, since A shows 0 road waits.
Robots respond to sanction cost, as the large behavioural shift under lambda 0 in D3 suggests, but a 10 s relaxation is much milder than removing sanctions.
C's 12.3 penalty points are roughly 0.5 x Minor overstays plus 1.5 x Major evictions attributed to C.
unknowns: The per-company split of release violations and blocking_guard evictions, which the observation table does not report.
Whether longer allowed holds raise blocked_s for A enough to lower its on-time rate below 0.93.
Whether this leg clears the min_improvement gate at all.

proposals.title: block_k 3 -> 2, measured in the busy regime with a sanction breakdown (second leg of the package)
proposals.rationale: A has the lowest on-time rate (0.93) and the most blocked seconds (847) without ever parking on the road, so it is the company harmed by others' road holding. In D1 and D2 block_k=2 raised on-time deliveries and cut p95 and max wait. What is new now: this is the first busy-regime measurement, and it comes with a current-rule sanction breakdown, where C pays 12.3 of 14.4 points and the blocking_guard Major evictions (4.2 x 1.5 = 6.3 points) fall on the road-parking companies B and C. I expect on-time deliveries to rise and p95 wait to fall, but the vote is likely to fail again (A yes, B no, C no) unless it is paired with the hold_limit relief above.

proposals.why_human: The human rejected block_k=2 on its own three times (D1 to D3) and asked that it be combined with a sanction change. It is proposed again only so that it is measured in the busy regime alongside proposal 1, as the second leg of a sequenced package that the one-step format forces. The human should decide whether this measurement, together with the sanction breakdown, is useful, and should not read it as a request to override a likely 1-2 vote. A per-company breakdown of the added violations is still not available from the table and must come from the measurement run.
assumptions: Lower block_k mainly evicts B and C robots parked at node 8, which reduces blocking of A.
The on-time gains seen in D1 and D2 carry over to the busy regime, despite the weaker 3/5 seed result in D3.
unknowns: The per-company and per-severity split of the added evictions under block_k=2, which the table does not provide.
How much of C's utility loss the hold_limit 70 s relief would offset if the two are stacked.
Whether the busy regime makes evictions more costly because robots return to the depot more often.
